title: Plan Atlas plan.yaml
description: Base arrays describe the system as it is today; every delta is an op inside changes[]. See SPEC.md §1.

systems.description: a system is several deployables (services) of one team that are built, run and changed together; the system map draws it as one card with its services inside

screens.description: what people see today: pages, modals, emails, pushes, prints, each with a screenshot and named regions; the to-be look is set by ops

interactions.description: Recorded screen interactions independent of system flows; shared navigation has several from screens or regions

user_journeys.description: Ordered paths through recorded interactions; every adjacent interaction connects through the same screen

graphs.description: federated GraphQL graphs: the gateway that composes and routes them

subgraphs.description: who contributes to a graph: each subgraph is served by one service

operations.description: the GraphQL documents the front end sends (queries and mutations); the query plan is derived from them

handlers.description: what runs when an endpoint is called, a message consumed, a schedule fires or a person acts

execution.description: Plain-language account of how the plan plays out; chapter 4 opens on it (How it plays out).

summary.description: markdown; explain how the design works, including what stays unchanged
markdown; the condition or outcome of this path

items.description: markdown; a material limitation or unresolved implementation detail

id_walk.description: flow:*, flow:*#step, gql:* (the steps that call the operation) or sg:* (the steps whose fan-out reaches the subgraph)

start.description: when delivery starts (YYYY-MM-DD); milestone due dates count from here

status.description: the plan's lifecycle: draft, review, approved (the room said yes). 'committed' is the old name for approved and still reads as it, with a warning

revisions.description: the revision ledger: one entry per proposed revision, oldest first; the newest approved entry is the canonical plan, snapshotted at plans/<slug>/revisions/<version>.yaml (tools/revision.mjs)

version.description: major.minor, e.g. 1.1; a scope change (goals, non-goals, milestones) is a new major

summary.description: one line: what this revision changes and why it is proposed

why.description: the proposer's reasoning in two or three sentences: what is wrong without it and why this way; the revision page leads with it

work.description: the proposer's word on what happens to work items the revision touches; the page infers the rest and marks it as inferred

action.description: rework: it changes (reopened when done); keep: it stands as it is; drop: it goes; new: it is added

note.description: what changes for it, in a sentence

by.description: who proposes it: team ids (team:…) or names

pr.description: the pull request that proposed it

approved_by.description: a GitHub handle such as @ryannel: whoever merged the pull request. One person answers for it; there is no sign-off across teams

rejected_by.description: a GitHub handle such as @ryannel: whoever closed the pull request

reason.description: why it was approved or rejected, in a sentence or two; a rejection without one leaves the history unexplained

approval_pr.description: the pull request that approved or rejected it; leave it out when that is the pull request that proposed it (`pr`)

repos.description: GitHub repos in scope, "org/name"; discovery starts here

colour.description: the team's slot in the app's thirteen-colour team palette (--team-1 to --team-13; 9 to 13 are drawn with a ring). Give a team the same slot in every plan, and no two teams in one plan the same while a slot is free

name.description: what people call the whole thing (often the repo or Backstage system name, in words)

does.description: the role of the whole system in plain words, ≤ 10 words; shown at the top of its card

summary.description: markdown; why these services belong together (shared repo, store, release). May cite [[id]]

sources.description: evidence it is one system: the Backstage spec.system line, the shared repo or the shared store

system.description: the system this deployable is part of; same team, same stage. The system map draws it as a row inside the system's card

does.description: its role in plain words a newcomer understands: what it does for the business, ≤ 10 words, sentence case, no jargon or code names. Shown on the system map card

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one

does.description: its role in plain words a newcomer understands: what it holds or carries, and for whom, ≤ 10 words, sentence case, no jargon or code names. Shown on the system map card

layer.description: kind: cache: where the layer sits on the cache path (outermost first)

granularity.description: kind: cache: whole responses, or per entity per subgraph fetch (Apollo Router entity caching)

keyed_by.description: kind: cache: what the key is made of, in words

purge.description: how an entry is emptied (surrogate key per sku, POST /invalidate)

invalidated_by.description: events that empty it (a shortcut; a flow step with purges: says who does it)

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one

key.description: part of the record's identity (primary key)

ref.description: a reference to another record: sch:* (its key) or sch:*#field

default.description: the value used when the field is left out

unique.description: no two records share the value

subgraphs.description: the subgraphs that resolve the field; required unless it is a key field

shareable.description: @shareable: two or more subgraphs resolve it

provides.description: @provides: fields of the return type this subgraph can resolve on the same fetch

requires.description: @requires: fields the gateway must fetch first and send along

override.description: @override: this field moves from another subgraph; percent = progressive override (null once the move is contracted)

reads.description: the record fields the owning subgraph reads

cache.description: data caches the resolver reads first

auth.description: who may read it; non-empty makes the field private

batched.description: overrides the subgraph's batching for this field

usage.description: registry field usage (evidence for a deprecation)

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one

graph.description: kind: graph-type only: the graph the type belongs to

root.description: kind: graph-type only: Query or Mutation

keys.description: kind: graph-type only: entity keys; `in` = the subgraphs that can be asked for the entity by that key (stub contributors included)

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one
evidence links; every as-is entity should have one
evidence links; every as-is entity should have one

key.description: the payload field the message is keyed by (its partition key), e.g. sku

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one
evidence links; every as-is entity should have one

screen.description: the screen (or region) the person is on when this step happens; makes the flow a UI journey

case.description: via gql: only: which cache case the flow narrates (hit = the outermost layer answers; miss = it misses and the next answers; cold = every layer misses)

purges.description: cache stores this step empties (the acting service must own them or have access)

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one
evidence links

due.description: target date for the milestone exit (YYYY-MM-DD)

github_issue.description: GitHub issue number in `repo`; written back by tools/export-issues.mjs, never authored by hand

issue_type.description: which issue template (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/<type>.yml) the exported issue uses; default task

status.description: deferred: deliberately left until after this plan; set decide_by as the date to revisit it

decider.description: the one team accountable for the call

decide_by.description: when a proposed decision must be accepted; when a deferred one is revisited

decided_on.description: when it was accepted or rejected

reversibility.description: one-way: costly or impossible to undo once shipped; two-way: can be changed later at low cost

supersedes.description: decisions this one replaces (they are marked superseded)

sources.description: evidence links
evidence links

accepted_by.description: with roam: accepted, the decision that knowingly accepts this risk as a trade-off

sources.description: evidence links

answered_by.description: the decision that answers this question; the question stays open until that decision is accepted

source.description: Where this fact lives: a GitHub permalink (blob/<sha>/path#L10-L20), a doc, a dashboard

label.description: shown instead of the URL; defaults to repo · path#line for GitHub blob links

note.description: markdown; what the reader will find there

domain.description: The business language and the path data takes, before any system detail. Rendered as chapter 2's opening screens.

summary.description: markdown; the narrative of how the domain's things are born and fan out. May cite [[id]]

stages.description: in the order data moves through them

terms.description: other words that mean the same thing in prose; the plural of name is added automatically

means.description: markdown; what it is in business terms. The first sentence is the tooltip. May cite [[id]]

born_in.description: the system of record: where its id is minted

as.description: verb phrase read as '<name> <as> <to>', e.g. 'is selected by'

at.description: the schema, field or store that holds it

introduced_by.description: set when the plan introduces the concept

name.description: a short verb or noun (Shop, Pick, Pay)

from.description: what this service reads from when no flow or topic access already says so (service, topic, interface or endpoint); drawn as a line on the system map

flows.description: optional; flows are otherwise placed by the stage of the service that acts in most of their steps

name.description: The control or trigger in plain words

note.description: What the local drawn example records; do not claim production evidence

interactions.description: Ordered interaction IDs; a repeat is permitted when a journey revisits a screen

assetPath.description: a file under the plan's folder, relative to plan.yaml (assets/product-page.png, mockups/walking.html); never a URL

regionBox.description: where the region sits on the image, in percent of its width/height (x,y = top-left corner)

region.description: A named part of a screen: a block the reader can point at (the price, the delivery line, the Pay button). Regions are what ops change and what steps point at

shows.description: markdown; what the region shows and where the data comes from; may cite [[id]]

reads.description: the records or fields the region displays

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one

screen.description: A screen a person sees: a page, a modal, an email, a push notification, a printed document. `image` is what it looks like (a screenshot today; a wireframe or export of the design in the to-be, set by a modify op). Steps point at the screen (or one of its regions) they happen on, which is how a flow becomes a UI journey

service.description: the kind: ui service that serves it (or the service that sends it, for an email or push)

route.description: the path or deep link, e.g. /p/{sku}, app://orders/{id}

device.description: what the image was taken on

image.description: screenshot of the screen today (as-is); a modify op sets the to-be picture (wireframe, design export)

figma.description: the design file or frame; usually set by a modify op in the to-be

mockup.description: a walking mockup: a static HTML file under the plan folder, opened at #<screen-id> (see tools/mockup.mjs and the plan-atlas-mockup skill)

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one

cacheUse.description: a cache layer attached to what it caches: on an operation, an edge/gateway override; on a graph field, a data cache the resolver reads first

ttl.description: seconds; on an operation an override of the derived max-age (give a reason)

key.description: what the layer keys on: free text, or { operation: id|hash, variables: all|[names], headers: [names] }

cacheControl.description: the cache hint the subgraph returns for the field (@cacheControl)

graph.description: A federated GraphQL graph. The gateway is an ordinary service; its team owns the graph

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one

subgraph.description: A subgraph: the unit of ownership in federation, served by one service

batching.description: request-scoped batching of entity lookups; none makes a list fetch an N+1

latency_ms.description: p50 of one fetch to this subgraph, in ms (a measurement, not a setting); lets the waterfall draw bars to scale

cache_control_default.description: seconds; the max-age a field without a hint takes (0 = uncacheable)

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one

operation.description: A GraphQL document the front end sends; paths, variables and the query plan are derived from it

screens.description: the screens or regions that issue it

cache.description: edge / gateway layers in front of it; ttl here is an override with a reason

plan_check.description: the registry's query plan, to check the derived one against

writes.description: a mutation's root resolver writes (checked against the root field's subgraph service)

sources.description: evidence links; every as-is entity should have one

trigger.description: when the front end sends it (fired when the page loads, when the button is pressed, …)

handlerOn.description: what starts the handler: an endpoint (api:), a consumed message (msg:), a schedule (job:<cron or name>) or an interaction on a screen (ui:)

origin.description: how the fact was made: read from code by a scan, seeded by hand for a demo, or written by a person

codeSource.description: a place in code; the permalink is derived from it

path.description: the file, from the repository root

commit.description: the commit the lines were read at

symbol.description: the function or class, e.g. PriceController.getPrice

result.description: what the caller gets, e.g. 404 not_found
